mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS increase, or FEDFUNDS rise is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% is associated with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 60-day forward returns through higher corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% over the next two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation from the pre-increase period (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or monthly PAYEMS growth <2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in HOUST (industrial production) by more than 3% in a month predicts reduced near-term business activity, which depresses S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate weaker earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >3% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified drop, or HOUST decline is ≤3%.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 5% signals supply-side weakness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the observed INDPRO declines, or INDPRO declines are <5% consecutively.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that prompts the Fed to hold rates steady, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, thus driving positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low UNRATE period, or UNRATE does not fall below 4% consecutively.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% in the next quarter suggest robust demand across sectors, which elevates S&P 500 60-day forward returns via higher earnings forecasts.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑ ≥2% and RSAFS ↑ ≥2% over the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive deviation (p ≥ 0.05), or either GDPC1 or RSAFS growth <2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of 1.5% in a month, accompanied by a decline in UNRATE to below 5%, signals wage pressure without labor slack, prompting cautious equity positioning and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by ≥1.5% while UNRATE < 5% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL rise <1.5% or UNRATE ≥5%.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent supply-side easing (indicated by a 4-month declining trend in INDPRO), S&P 500 5-day forward returns tend to be negative due to muted growth expectations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the observed INDPRO downtrend, or INDPRO shows a rising trend.
